entities.summary:
John of Procida was an Italian medieval physician and diplomat.

Born around 1250 in Procida, Kingdom of Sicily (present-day Italy), John of Procida rose to prominence as a renowned physician and advisor to various monarchs, including King Frederick II of Sicily and King Charles I of Anjou. He played a crucial role in the development of medical knowledge during the Middle Ages.

One of his most notable achievements was the translation of several medical texts from Arabic into Latin, which significantly contributed to the advancement of medicine in Europe. His work in this field has been recognized as a key factor in the spread of Islamic medical knowledge during the Crusades.

Despite his significant contributions to medicine and diplomacy, John of Procida's life remains somewhat shrouded in mystery, with limited historical records available about his personal life and later years.

The legacy of John of Procida can be seen in the continued development of medical knowledge during the Renaissance period, which built upon the foundations laid by this Italian physician.
